successCases.reasoning: Stress 99 is below threshold; full stress with timer 2 is ineligible. Neither pass removes cards, so nonempty inactive backing slots survive. Inactive attacker and counter are not normalized; no TurnEnd timer decrement occurs.

The first entry deals 200 + 100 = 300 HP damage and 20 requested stress; team 1 reaches -100. The first winner check stops before its still-eligible second entry and before any crumble update. Even the intentionally stale level 2 for healthy team 0 remains unchanged.

Calm team 0 enters first without damage. Team 1 remains eligible and enters second, reducing team 0 from 200 to -100 and adding 20 stress. Crumble is calculated before the second winner check: 1100 / 250 truncates to 4, clamped to level 3. Timer 4 remains unchanged because TurnEnd is outside scope.

Both start eligible, so the first pass picks team 1. Its timer then prevents reselection; the second pass still uses priority [1, 0] and picks team 0. Neither calm nor bold changes the inactive combo checkpoint.

Compose at active slot 1 reduces selected team 0 to stress 50 and suppresses its Reckless damage. Removing the counter clears nonempty inactive slots as well. Team 1 retains stress 100 and timer 0, so it is selected and enters calmly on pass two.

The first Compose leaves team 1 eligible. In the second pass team 0 has both active Agitate at slot 1 and Compose at slot 2, but canReflect is false, so only Compose is searched and removed. No redirect, Reckless damage, timer update or third pass occurs.

Reading the current hand at increasing slots hits original slots 0, 2, 4 and 6. The four manually assigned damages are 100, 200, 150 and 100; stress increments are 6, 13, 10 and 6. Total damage 550 leaves HP 450 and stress 35. Only after all four hits does the winner check allow the second no-entry pass and crumble to level 2.

The second hit is lethal, but the whole source loop still takes the third and fourth draws, removes their cards and reaches counter 4. Stress uses each requested damage even when the HP floor reduces actual loss. First-pass victory then skips pass two and all crumble updates.

Pass one hits cards 1 and 3 with attack 100 and jitter 0, 1, totaling 302; team 1 stays at full stress until its own entry resets it. Pass two uses team 1 attack 70 and its own jitter 2, 3, totaling 218 and adding 4 + 9 stress to team 0. Nested draw indexes stay local at 0, 1 in each component receipt. The outer offsets are recorded separately.

Each forward scan attacks original slots 0, 2, 4 and 6, leaving three topic cards. Each hit deals 70 HP and 4 stress, so each target loses 280 HP. Team 1's full stress is clamped during pass one then reset at its own entry; team 0 receives 16 stress during pass two. Both levels become 1. Four draws per pass reaches the eight-draw outer admission bound.

Agitate redirects entry from team 0 to team 1 without rechecking team 1's zero stress. Removing Agitate first compacts the Timid hand to [0, 1, 3, -1, -1, -1, -1]. The combo hits card 1 at current slot 1 and skips card 3 after it shifts into that already-visited slot. Its component-local originalSlot is 1 because provenance begins at the post-entry combo input. The sole hit uses entered team 1's attack 70 plus pass-one jitter 2, not team 0's attack 227. Team 0 ends at HP 928 and stress 50 + 4 = 54.

Neither pass enters anger. Crumble is nevertheless run after the second pass: healthy team 0 changes downward from stored level 3 to 0 and sets its flag true; team 1's computed level remains 1 and preserves its already-true flag. No flag reset or monotonic-only level rule is introduced.

refusalCases.reasoning: The outer composition admits only inactive combos; it must not attempt to reinterpret an active stale checkpoint as a newly entered Timid combo.
External entry HP is 1 through 1000 even though internal kernel results may reach zero or -100.
Both team-indexed attacks are validated up front, including the attack that would never be used in this drawless first-pass kill.
The delegated whole mutable-hand scan requires four draws. No partial entry, three-hit state or receipt is returned.
Three well-formed draws fit the outer four-draw limit, but the whole first combo consumes exactly two. The component, not a duplicate outer hand scan, detects the unused draw.
A pass that does not activate a combo must have an empty draw array.
A well-formed but unused draw in the skipped second pass is not silently accepted; the local first-pass result is discarded.
Both pass arrays are parsed before either kernel is called. Value 5 is invalid for a bound-5 draw, so this fails before first-pass damage rather than reaching unused-second-pass-draws.
Pass one's detached work does not weaken atomicity: failure during the second combo returns no first-pass state, nested receipt or draw audit.
The outer pass-local admission limit is four draws, irrespective of their individual validity.
The whole composition's admitted profile always requires the explicit generic identity-hook assertion.
Stored levels are explicitly bounded 0 through 3; the outer parser does not normalize them.
The complete policy must equal the exported policy, not merely share its identifier.
